items.title: Eric Alexander interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: "You know we’re not all Mozart or Charlie Parker." / "if I give one kid “Charlie Parker with Strings,” and say this is the only thing you’re allowed to listen for six months. I want you to learn every note that he plays"

ctx.x: Okay. You don’t have the fall back on.

No. And I’m not saying that’s a bad thing. And I suppose I shouldn’t use myself necessarily as a reference for everyone. But I just really believe that there are many people who share a similar level of talent. You know Harold [Mabern] was talking yesterday about 97 percent perspiration, 3 percent inspiration? I believe there are many, many people that are gifted, at least to a certain level. You know we’re not all Mozart or Charlie Parker. But there are many people with a certain level of musical talent, a gift…
The Thelonious Monk competition, when you came in second place one year I guess, did that do anything for you ostensibly? Open any doors for you or —
